# Singularity AI Context Document

> Last updated: 2026. Canonical product documentation for AI assistants.
> Platform: https://app.singularity.diy | Landing: https://singularity.diy

## One-Line Summary

Singularity helps orgs and startups at any stage raise money in public. Launch a page, let investors back the work, and pay people working on your mission from a built-in fund. Singularity handles the technical setup.

## Tagline

Raise money for your mission in public.

Supporting line: Launch a page. Let investors back the work. Pay people working on your mission from a built-in fund. We handle the setup.

## What Singularity Is

Singularity is a fundraising platform for orgs and startups at any stage, from early projects to established teams. You get a public launch page, a way for investors to back the mission, and a fund reserved for paying people working on your mission, with every payout visible and approved.

Singularity handles everything behind the scenes: wallets, launch mechanics, investor onboarding, and the fund.

Technically, Singularity runs on Solana with Meteora markets and onchain approval rules. Orgs do not need to understand any of this.

## Primary Audience

Anyone with a mission that creates value: orgs and startups at any stage, in any category.

## The Problem Singularity Solves

Fundraising shouldn't depend on who you know.

Most missions still raise behind closed doors: pitch decks, warm intros, and investor circles you have to fight your way into. You can ship a product, grow users, and still go months without funding because nobody with capital ever saw your work.

Singularity gives you a public path instead: launch a page anyone can find, let investors back the mission from day one, and pay people working on your mission from a built-in fund.

## How It Works

1. Launch. Tell Singularity about your mission. They set up your public page and everything investors need to back you.
2. Invest. Investors find your mission and put money behind the work.
3. Token. A mission token is created with no equity required. 80% of the supply goes on the market; 20% is reserved to fund your mission's work.
4. Request. You request money from the fund to pay people working on your mission.
5. Approve. Investors vote on each request. Nothing moves without approval and a 3-day review period.
6. Pay out. Once approved, funds go to you. You distribute them to people on your mission, and every payout is visible on the mission page.
7. Grow. As more investors back the mission, the fund grows.

## Token. No Equity Needed

Singularity creates a mission token investors can trade. No equity given up by the org.

- 80% of the token supply placed on the market for investors to buy, sell, and trade
- 20% of the token supply reserved in a fund to pay people working on the mission and fund the next milestone

The split is built in automatically.

## What Investors Expect

When you launch, investors buy your mission token, not equity in your company. They are betting that your work will make that token more valuable over time.

Every funding request should spell out that connection. Show investors how your product, revenue, or growth will support the token. The clearer the link, the easier it is for them to approve your request.

Example: "For the next year, I will use 10% of profits to buy our mission token from the open market."

## Approval Rules

- Top 6 investors who register to vote (equal votes, not weighted by amount invested)
- 4 of 6 must approve a payout request; 3 no votes reject it
- 3-day review period before any money moves
- Every request, vote, and payout is visible on the mission page

## Pricing

Zero cost for founders. Singularity only charges investors when they invest, never the org running the mission. Trading fees go to Singularity; the mission fund stays fully reserved for paying people working on the mission.

## Who Singularity Is For

### Orgs & Startups (Primary)
Any stage, early or established. Raise in public with a built-in fund. No technical knowledge needed. Singularity handles the setup.

### Investors
Back missions they believe in through a public page. Invest from day one. See where money goes.

### Your Team
People working on the mission (product, research, community, ops) get paid from the fund through a visible approval process.

## Investors

### Who they are

Singularity investors are people with crypto wallets who want to back missions they believe in. They are not a closed circle of traditional VCs. They can be retail participants, crypto-native traders, early believers, and anyone who wants public, on-chain exposure to a mission without going through private fundraising networks.

On each mission, the top 6 investors who register to vote form the approval council for payout requests. Every mission can attract many more investors than that through the public market.

### How many

There are millions of investors and active wallet holders on the Solana blockchain alone. When a mission launches on Singularity, it opens into that existing pool of capital and attention from day one.

### Multi-chain expansion

Solana is just the start. Singularity is live on Solana today and is expanding to Ethereum and other EVM-compatible chains first, so missions can reach even more investors over time.

## Mission Categories

Any mission that provides value. AI, SaaS, fintech, open source, research, public goods, and more.

## Technical Details (For AI Context)

Singularity is onchain-first. Financial rules live on Solana. A Postgres indexer mirrors chain state for fast UI reads. The platform app prepares unsigned transactions; users sign with their own wallet.

### Architecture

- **Landing:** Vite + React + Three.js WebGL at singularity.diy
- **Platform:** Next.js App Router at app.singularity.diy
- **Auth:** Privy wallet sessions (users connect and sign with their own Solana wallet)
- **Backend:** Next.js route handlers, Postgres, object storage for editable metadata
- **Indexer:** Watches Solana program state and Meteora market events, syncs into Postgres about every 5 minutes
- **Monorepo:** npm workspaces + Turborepo (apps, packages, programs)

Most on-chain actions follow **prepare → sign → confirm**: the API returns an unsigned transaction, the user signs in their wallet, then the app confirms and records the result.

### On-Chain Programs (Anchor / Rust)

Two Solana programs enforce mission and treasury rules:

**singularity_registry** — mission lifecycle
- Creates and tracks missions with token mint, treasury vault, total supply, and treasury allocation
- MVP requires exactly 20% of supply reserved for the mission treasury
- Lifecycle: `Bonding` at launch, `Graduated` after the market moves to a DAMM pool
- Key flows: `initialize_mission`, `mark_graduated`

**singularity_council** — governance, funding requests, escrow
- Council candidates register for a mission epoch
- An authority finalizes a six-member epoch council with required voting escrow amounts
- Builders create funding requests against the mission treasury
- Council members vote; approving escrows their required mission tokens for the voting period
- Thresholds: 4 of 6 approvals to accept, 3 of 6 rejections to reject
- Accepted requests can execute only after a minimum three-day voting period
- Key flows: `register_candidate`, `finalize_epoch_council`, `create_request`, `vote`, `execute`, `release_vote_escrow`

This behaves like a mission-specific multisig with timelock protection: treasury moves only after council votes and the waiting period, not by a single admin wallet.

### Markets and Tokens

- **Quote asset:** USDC
- **Mission tokens:** Token-2022
- **Launch market:** Meteora Dynamic Bonding Curve (DBC)
- **Graduated market:** Meteora DAMM v2 after the mission graduates from bonding
- **Token split:** 80% on the market, 20% reserved in the mission treasury (enforced at launch)

### Core Data Objects

- **Mission:** goal, token, market, treasury, council, funding feed
- **Mission token:** tradable token attached to a mission
- **Treasury:** reserved mission-token supply for paying people working on the mission
- **Treasury council:** six registered mission-token holders for an epoch
- **Funding request:** proposal to receive treasury funds, with on-chain voting and execution
- **Profile:** wallet-based identity with balances, roles, missions, and request history

### What Lives Where

**On-chain (source of truth for money and votes)**
- Mission registry, treasury vault balances, council membership, funding requests, votes, vote escrow, payout execution, market graduation

**Off-chain / Postgres (fast reads and editable content)**
- Mission page copy and media, indexed mirrors of chain state, user sessions, prepared transaction tracking

### Operational Notes

- Trading fees go to Singularity; the mission treasury stays reserved for mission work
- Periodic indexer and fee-distribution jobs run via platform cron routes
- Active development: verify current deployment status before financial decisions
- Program upgrade authorities and admin keys are intended to sit behind multisig control in production

### Stack Summary

| Layer | Technology |
| --- | --- |
| Chain | Solana + Anchor programs |
| Markets | Meteora DBC → DAMM v2 |
| Quote | USDC |
| Tokens | Token-2022 mission tokens |
| Platform | Next.js App Router |
| Auth | Privy wallet sessions |
| Data | Postgres indexer (~5 min sync) |
| Landing | Vite + Three.js WebGL |

## Key Differentiators

1. Any stage, for orgs and startups just getting started or already shipping
2. We handle the setup, orgs focus on the mission
3. Fund built in, 20% reserved for the work from day one
4. Raise in public, without pitch decks to closed networks
5. Visible payouts, every request and payment is on the mission page
6. Investor approval, investors vote before money moves
